name: Sanjay Ghemawat
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned MS from MIT at 24 and was a PhD student. His foundational work on MapReduce, GFS, and Bigtable began at Google starting age 33.
early_history_summary: Born in West Lafayette, Indiana, and grew up in Kota, Rajasthan, India. Did not touch a computer until age 17 at Cornell. Earned BS from Cornell (1987), MS from MIT (1990), and PhD from MIT (1995) under Barbara Liskov. Worked at DEC Systems Research Center before joining Google in 1999.
family_context_summary: Father was a botany professor; mother was a homemaker. Brother Pankaj became the youngest faculty member ever awarded tenure at Harvard Business School. A bookish family.

name: Amit Singhal
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned MS from University of Minnesota Duluth at 23 and was a PhD student at Cornell. His major work rewriting Google's search algorithms began at age 32 in 2000.

Earned BS from IIT Roorkee (1989), MS from University of Minnesota Duluth (1991), and PhD from Cornell (1996) under Gerard Salton, a pioneer in information retrieval. Worked at AT&T Labs before joining Google in 2000 as employee 176.

name: Yann LeCun
milestone_by_age_26: Proposed and published an early version of the error backpropagation algorithm at the COGNITIVA conference in Paris in June 1985, at age 24, a foundational contribution to neural network learning.
early_history_summary: LeCun grew up in the suburbs of Paris with an engineer father who fostered early tinkering with electronics and mechanics. He attended ESIEE Paris, a selective engineering school, and began independent machine learning research as an undergraduate. During his PhD at Universite Pierre et Marie Curie, he developed and published an early form of backpropagation, initially proposing the algorithm during his DEA work in 1983-1984.
family_context_summary: Father was an engineer with interests in electronics and mechanics, which he passed on to LeCun during a boyhood of tinkering. Inspired by HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey as a young boy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's engineering background provided early exposure to electronics and mechanics, relevant to LeCun's later work in computing and neural networks.
primary_early_advantage_tags: engineering family, early tinkering, independent research, French engineering education, neural networks
evidence_summary: LeCun grew up in suburban Paris with an engineer father who fostered early tinkering with electronics and mechanics. He attended ESIEE Paris, a selective engineering school, and began independent machine learning research as an undergraduate inspired by HAL 9000. By age 24, during his PhD at Universite Pierre et Marie Curie, he had proposed and published an early version of the backpropagation algorithm at the COGNITIVA 1985 conference, a foundational contribution later cited in the landmark Rumelhart et al. 1986 Nature paper. His early advantage came from domain proximity through his father's engineering background and self-driven deep exploration of a then-unfashionable field.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in the suburbs of Paris to an engineer father with interests in electronics and mechanics; grew up tinkering with technology and was inspired by HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
current_position: Co-founded Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs in December 2025 after serving as Chief AI Scientist at Meta (2013-2025); Jacob T. Schwartz Professor at NYU Courant Institute; Turing Award laureate (2018).

trajectory.event: Published an early version of the backpropagation algorithm at the COGNITIVA conference in Paris.
Completed PhD in computer science at Universite Pierre et Marie Curie with a thesis on connectionist learning models.
Joined AT&T Bell Labs as a research scientist, where he developed convolutional neural networks (LeNet) for handwriting recognition.
Became head of the Image Processing Research Department at AT&T Labs-Research.
Joined NYU as a professor of computer science at the Courant Institute.
Named Director of AI Research at Facebook (later Meta).
Co-recipient of the ACM Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for work on deep learning.
Co-founded Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs after leaving Meta.

name: Geoffrey Hinton
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned BA from Cambridge at 23, worked briefly as a carpenter, and began PhD studies at Edinburgh at 25. His landmark backpropagation paper was published in 1986 at age 39.
early_history_summary: Born in Wimbledon, London, into a family with deep mathematical and scientific heritage (great-great-grandfather George Boole, father entomologist Howard Hinton). Earned BA in Experimental Psychology from Cambridge (1970), worked as a carpenter, then pursued PhD in AI at Edinburgh (1972-1978) despite constant discouragement from advisors who thought neural networks were a dead end.
family_context_summary: Born into a family with a strong background in mathematics and science. Great-great-grandparents were George Boole and Mary Everest Boole. Father Howard was a noted British entomologist. Related to surveyor George Everest. Hinton said growing up with such a background 'felt like pressure.'
parent_family_domain_summary: Deep family heritage in mathematics and science, including George Boole whose work underpins computer science. Father was a distinguished entomologist. This created intellectual pressure and domain familiarity but not direct neural network expertise.
evidence_summary: Hinton grew up in a family with extraordinary mathematical and scientific heritage, including George Boole as a great-great-grandfather. He earned his BA at 23, took time off as a carpenter, and started his PhD at 25. His career-defining backpropagation work came at 39, long after the age-26 cutoff.

name: Yoshua Bengio
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned B.Eng from McGill at 22 and MSc at 24, was a PhD student at McGill at 26. His foundational deep learning publications and faculty appointment at Universite de Montreal came after age 27.
early_history_summary: Born in Paris, France, to Jewish parents who had emigrated from Morocco and embraced 1960s counterculture. Family moved to Montreal when Yoshua was 12. Self-described 'typical nerd' who bought an Atari 800 and Apple II with his brother Samy. Earned B.Eng (1986), MSc (1988), and PhD (1991) from McGill, then postdocs at MIT and Bell Labs before joining Universite de Montreal faculty in 1993.

name: Andrew Ng
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned BS from CMU at 21 and MS from MIT at 22, was a PhD student at UC Berkeley at 26. His major work (Google Brain, Coursera, Stanford AI Lab directorship) began after age 30.

name: Sebastian Thrun

name: Fei-Fei Li
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; immigrated to the US at 16, earned BA from Princeton at 26 (1999). Her career-defining work creating ImageNet began around 2009 at age 36.

Created ImageNet around 2009, co-directed Stanford Human-Centered AI Institute, and co-founded World Labs.

name: Ian Goodfellow
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; was a PhD student at Universite de Montreal under Yoshua Bengio at 26. His career-defining invention of GANs came in 2014 at approximately age 27-29 (Wikipedia lists birth year as 1987, CSV lists 1985).

name: Andrej Karpathy
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned BSc from University of Toronto at 23 and MSc from UBC at 25, was a PhD student at Stanford at 26. His career-defining work (CS231n, OpenAI, Tesla Autopilot) came after age 26.

Pursued PhD at Stanford under Fei-Fei Li (completed 2015), designed and taught CS231n, then joined OpenAI and later became Director of AI at Tesla.
